root_motivation: The operator (Joe / the Opus operator seat) cannot trust "gate green" to mean "main CI green": a timing test written with a literal budget passes on RedBaron at load 2 and fails on a GitHub runner, and nothing in the repo refuses the literal form. Leg 18 five whys, level 5: "timing assertions are written per test with literal budgets instead of one harness-owned budget that every wall-clock assertion must use — and nothing enforces 'must use'". Evidence: 23 assertions outside the macros at b8d4732 (`git grep -nE 'assert!\(.*(elapsed|Duration|p95|_ms|millis|as_millis)' origin/main -- tests/ | grep -v perf_budget`), 16 files already using the macros, `flakelint_ac07` `ALLOW` naming 4 files "still to be wrapped".
user_persona: An agent (customer) that calls host.webhook_inbox.create once, pastes the url into a sender and shows its user the push event in the same session; the truth-tier integration_specialist persona whose gold is reachable in 4 calls; Operator Joe reading the digest.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a scratch tests tree with a file that prints `perf skipped (load)` by hand and asserts `p95 < Duration::from_millis(50)` on a later line (the pre-#176 `docsearch_ac11:53-58` shape), When `scripts/timing-lint.py` runs, Then exit 1 naming that file:line and token; Given the same assertion wrapped in `perf_budget!`, Then exit 0.

Given a scratch file whose `perf_budget!` block is followed by a separate bare `assert!(t.elapsed() < Duration::from_millis(5))`, When the script runs, Then it names the bare line (the file-level `src.contains("perf_budget!")` check in `flakelint_ac07` passes this file today).

Given a scratch `tests/common/mod.rs` exporting `macro_rules! my_budget` under a `/// timing-helper` doc line, When a test asserts elapsed inside `my_budget!{…}`, Then exit 0; Given the doc line removed, Then exit 1 — the allow set comes from the harness file, and the script contains no helper name.

Given a `deadline_budget!(100, { body })` whose body sleeps 150 ms, When run with `MCPHOST_PERF_SKIP` unset, Then it panics with `deadline_budget: elapsed=… budget=100ms`; Given `MCPHOST_PERF_SKIP=1`, Then it passes (budget ×3) and never prints `perf skipped`.

Given mcphost at this PRD's landing commit, When `scripts/timing-lint.py tests` runs, Then exit 0 with `0 offenders`, and `grep -c 'const ALLOW\|const PATTERNS' tests/flakelint_ac07_timing_tests_use_perf_budget.rs` is 0 and `tests/flake-lint-allow.txt` has no `single-shot-perf` entry.

Given the 4 former `ALLOW` files and the 9 budget sites named in Technical considerations, When `cargo test` runs each converted file with and without `MCPHOST_PERF_SKIP=1`, Then every test passes and no budget number changed (`git diff` shows the same millisecond literals).
Given a scratch file asserting `body["p95_ms"].is_number()`, When the script runs, Then exit 0 (a JSON field name is not a wall-clock token).

Given the first daemon gate on the landed tree, When its `flake-audit` producer runs, Then the gate log carries `timing-lint: 0 offenders` and the run reaches land (Live; evidence: `grep -l 'timing-lint: 0 offenders' /mnt/data/wm-build/runs/*/gate-receipts/flake-audit-attempt*.log | head -1`)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned: first daemon gate on the landed tree carries `timing-lint: 0 offenders` in its flake-audit log.

additional.signup_is_not_remembered: R3 says signup or host.redeem, but tests/sessbind_* pin signup followed by key-less behavior; only host.redeem is recorded (AC4's own scenario).

five_whys_trace.q: Why did the 10-09 webhook-inbox session make seven calls and never publish?
five_whys_trace.a: The recipe was three host steps with the hook URL only in step 2, and key-less quickstart answers repeated after a successful redeem.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did a key-less call after redeem not work?
five_whys_trace.a: /mcp is stateless, so no session carries the redeem; the next key-less call implicit-signed-up a second tenant.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the fix key on the peer?
five_whys_trace.a: IP + User-Agent hash is the only identity the stateless handler has across those calls; a 10-minute memory turns the second tenant into a named refusal.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Peer hash = IP+UA or IP only?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: IP+UA (the PRD default), hashed; recorded in the PR.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which quota gates create: event_triggers_max or schedules_max?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Both are checked before anything is created; event_triggers_max counts event + message + webhook triggers, so the free plan's 3 trips plan_limit first (data.limit 3).
